data.description: Ruling 2026-08-14 (sequence/org-settings-design.md iteration 3): one audit substrate projected three ways, never three logs. The substrate exists — audit_log (migration 0006, src/lib/audit.ts). (1) Instrument the org-level writers that do not yet record: invite mint/claim/revoke, member removal (with what was revoked), token create/revoke, org default changes, ownership transfer — some of these writers are being built by MRQ-207 and the governance ticket in parallel; instrument what exists on main and leave a named seam the parallel tickets call. (2) Org admin lens: reverse-chron log of admin actions (design: prototype v1.15 #org/activity) — steady-state home is an org-settings tab (MRQ-207 shell; standalone route if 207 unmerged, noted in PR). (3) Person lens: the person record activity feed merges audit rows touching that person with the existing annotations/history. (4) Submission lens: a timeline on the submission record — submitted, routed, reviewed, decided, reversed, re-accepted, mail sent — each with author and timestamp; extend the existing ContentHistory/history machinery rather than inventing parallel storage. Server-side pagination; R7 budgets; tests per lens.

> ## ⛔ PAUSED — DO NOT MERGE
>
> Paused by the fleet merge captain on 2026-08-14, for size and hour, **not for
> quality**. Four blocking findings from an adversarial review, all invisible to
> CI on a green gate. Head `75d56772` is rebased onto `f83406e8` with a verified
> FK counter, so whoever resumes starts from a current base — the four findings
> below are the whole remaining scope. Read finding 3 first; it is a live
> cross-tenant leak.

## One append-only log, three lenses

`audit_log` is the substrate. Nothing here creates a second event table, and no lens
stores a feed — every one of the three is a query over the same rows, projected by one
shared server-side copy module so the page, the API and an agent read a given row the
same way.

---

# The four blocking findings

Every one of these passes CI today. None of them fails a test. That is the point: the
review found them by reading, and the gate was green through all of it.

## 1 — Paging is incorrect under append, and the dedupe hides it

**Where:** `src/lib/org-activity.ts` (`orgActivityPage`, `personFeedPage` — `LIMIT ? OFFSET ?`),
`src/lib/history.ts` (`recordTimelinePage` — same), and the three callers:
`src/ui/settings/OrgActivityPage.tsx`, `src/ui/people/PersonDrawer.tsx`,
`src/ui/submissions/SubmissionRecordPage.tsx`.

**Reproduce:** read page one of the organization log (50 rows). Have any organizer mint
an invite — one row lands at the top. Read page two. Every row's index has shifted by
one, so the row that was last on page one is now first on page two.

**Wrong result, two ways.** `PersonDrawer` and `SubmissionRecordPage` call `appendUnseen`
over the *older* pages only, excluding page one, so that boundary row is appended a
second time and rendered twice with a duplicate key. `OrgActivityPage` does dedupe
against everything shown — and that is the worse case, because the duplicate disappears
while **the row that was pushed off the boundary is never fetched at all**. The lens then
prints `43 of 43 · Complete` over 42 distinct rows. A log that silently omits and calls
itself complete is worse than one that visibly repeats.

**Why no test catches it:** every existing test reads pages against a table nobody is
writing to. The missing test is a concurrent-append regression — read page one, insert a
row, read page two, assert nothing lost and nothing duplicated.

**The fix is structural, not a patch.** `appendUnseen` treats a symptom of offset paging;
offset paging over an append-only table is wrong by construction. Page by a stable
`(created_at, id)` keyset cursor instead, or freeze a snapshot for the paging session.
Keyset is cheap here: the ids are ULIDs, the tie-break is already `created_at DESC, id DESC`
in every query, and the indexes (`idx_audit_org_created`, `idx_audit_entity_created`)
already lead with the cursor columns.

## 2 — "Append-only" is false, in the audit log itself

**Where:** `src/lib/events/delete-event.ts:254-269` — `UPDATE audit_log SET actor_person_id = NULL`
on the remove-demo path.

**Reproduce:** run the demo removal against rows authored by demo people. Existing audit
rows lose their author.

**Why it matters:** this PR's own title and body call the log append-only, and an audit
log's entire value is that it can be trusted later. The moment it is known to mutate,
every row in it is weaker — including the rows this feature adds.

**Note on ownership:** the `UPDATE` is **pre-existing code on `main`**; this PR did not
write it. The *claim* that contradicts it is this PR's. So the contradiction is this
PR's to resolve, either way.

**Decide it consciously, then do one:** (a) preserve authorship and satisfy remove-demo
another way; or (b) keep the null-out, **stop calling the log append-only**, and document
exactly which path mutates it and why — in the PR body and beside the code. What is not
acceptable is the claim and the `UPDATE` coexisting silently.

## 3 — Cross-tenant leak in the person feed *(read this one first)*

**Where:** `src/lib/org-activity.ts` — `personFeedPage(db, personId, …)` takes **no
`orgId`**, and all three UNION arms filter on person/entity id alone.
`src/routes/people.routes.ts` calls `requirePerson(orgId, personId)` and *then* performs
that unscoped read.

**Reproduce:** two organizations on one instance. Insert an Org B audit row whose
`entity_type = 'person'` and whose `entity_id` names an Org A person P. Open P's drawer in
Org A. The Org B row is in the feed.

**Why it is real and not theoretical:** `audit_log.entity_id` is unconstrained text with
no foreign key, so nothing prevents a row in one org from naming another org's id. This
is check-then-read: the authorization and the query are two separate facts, so the check
can be right while the read is still wrong.

**The fix — put the predicate on the query, on every arm.** One unscoped arm is the whole
leak: the audit arm via `org_id` (or its event's org), `person_events` via
`person_events.org_id`, `outbox` via its event/org. Passing an `orgId` parameter through
while leaving any arm unfiltered fixes nothing. Add a **second-org negative control**: seed
the Org B row above, read Org A's feed, assert absent. A happy-path test passes today and
will pass forever.

## 4 — The timeline asserts a send that may never have happened

**Where:** `src/lib/activity-copy.ts` maps `submission.message_sent` → "Message sent" and
`submission.decision_resent` → "Decision email resent". But `src/routes/comms.routes.ts`
**queues** the mail and writes that audit row before the consumer runs, and
`src/jobs/cascade/decisions.ts` (`resendSubmissionDecision`) writes "resent" even when
`after.outbox_inserted` is `false`.

**Reproduce:** demo-mode send to a speaker who is not on the demo allowlist. The outbox is
suppressed. The timeline still reads "Message sent". **This is live in the demo today** —
the allowlist is exactly why an outbox gets suppressed.

**Why it matters:** an organizer reading "Message sent" will not chase the speaker who
never received it. That is precisely the failure this product exists to prevent, delivered
by the feature meant to prevent it.

**The fix:** say *queued* at queue time and *sent* only when the consumer records an actual
sent fact. Two moments, two truths. A single row that changes state collides with finding
2 — you cannot both claim append-only and mutate the row — so **2 and 4 must be decided
together**.

---

# The delegator's own read, for whoever resumes

Verbatim, because it is the honest version and a starting point beats starting from scratch:

- **3 is the one I would fix first and the one I most regret.** `audit_log.entity_id` is
  unconstrained text, `person_events` carries `org_id` and I did not use it, and I leaned
  on `requirePerson` as if a check were a filter. It is a leak, not a smell.
- **1 is correct as a class argument.** `appendUnseen` removes the duplicate and leaves the
  omission, and a lens that can say "Complete" while short is worse than one that
  duplicates, because nobody can see it. Keyset on `(created_at, id)` is the honest fix and
  the ULID ids make it available cheaply.
- **4 I half-knew.** I deliberately wrote `submission.decision_mail_queued` as *queued* for
  exactly this reason, then left the pre-existing `message_sent` / `decision_resent` copy
  asserting *sent*. Applying the rule in one place and not the other is worse than not
  knowing it.
- **2:** the `UPDATE` in `delete-event.ts` is pre-existing `main` code, but the claim is
  mine, in the title and the body, so the contradiction is mine to resolve either way.

Findings 1 and 3 are both "the query must carry the invariant" fixes rather than patches.
Do them awake.

---

# A durable lesson: a pinned counter cannot survive a rebase

`scripts/schema-verify.mjs` pins the exact foreign-key count. During the rebase onto
`f83406e8`, **git dropped this branch's counter bump as "patch contents already upstream"** —
because #259's own +1 had already moved `main` to 106, the same number this branch's commit
was changing it to. This branch's delta was silently absorbed into another branch's result.

Merged as-is, the real graph would have been 107 while the assertion said 106 — and it
would have gone **red on `main`**, where the branch that reds is not the branch that broke
it.

**So: a pinned counter must be recomputed and re-verified from the tool every time the base
moves.** `npm run check:schema` reporting `107 foreign keys` against the applied migrations
is the only reason the number here is right; arithmetic from the old base would have agreed
with the wrong answer.

**This generalises past this ticket: any pinned count whose value collides with another
branch's result is invisible to git.**

---

- Green at this head: three typechecks; `check:schema` (53 tables / 134 indexes / 107 FKs /

- An earlier lattice code review returned **PASS** and its six minor findings are already

## What was built (unchanged by the pause)

Migration `0021` makes `audit_log.event_id` nullable and adds `org_id`, with a CHECK that
every row is scoped to at least one — because org-level actions (invites, tokens, organizer
removal, ownership) belong to no conference, and a freshly claimed instance has an

`src/lib/org-activity.ts` is the named seam MRQ-207 and MRQ-212 call. **The org lens reads
by `org_id`, not by an action allowlist**, so their actions appear the day they ship;
`org.defaults_changed` and `org.ownership_transferred` already read correctly and are

Instrumented writers: invite mint/revoke/claim, instance claim, organizer removal (in the

grants, never the secret), plus `submission.received`, `submission.routed`,

**Placement:** MRQ-207's org shell is not on `main`, so the admin lens ships standalone at
`/org/activity` with no sidebar row; 207 mounts the same component as the Activity tab.

data.reason: PAUSED by the fleet merge captain (reversible if the operator overrules). PR #267 is green and rebased but carries four review findings, two structural — decide whether to resume it, and when; the four findings with reproductions are in the board comment above.

data.body:
DESIGN RULINGS for the four paused findings (org-settings design authority; resume needs no further design input):

(1) Offset paging → keyset on (created_at, id): ENDORSED. Correctness fix, no design tension. 'Complete' may only render when the keyset read returns fewer rows than asked.

(2) 'Append-only' vs delete-event.ts nulling actor_person_id: RULED — append-only means the row and its story survive; referential links may be severed by lawful deletions. Resolution: denormalize the actor label (name snapshot at write time) onto the audit row, so nulling the FK keeps displayed attribution. This is the same principle as organizer removal ('their work stays on the record, with their name') applied to the substrate. The existing nulling behavior is then correct, not a contradiction — and the lens never renders an anonymous action for an attributed one.

(3) personFeedPage unscoped by org: MUST-FIX before any merge — cross-tenant read. check-then-read via requirePerson as the finding proposes. Not a design question.

(4) 'Message sent' for queued/suppressed mail: RULED — the timeline mirrors outbox state with three distinct words: queued / suppressed (demo-safe) / sent, and 'sent' renders only from a real sent record. Honesty-is-respect (PHILOSOPHY §1) applied literally. (2) and (4) together: both reduce to 'the log tells the truth at write time and the lens repeats it without improving it.'

Resume when the merge captain reopens the window; the pause was size-and-hour, and these rulings clear the design half of the handoff.

data.body:
INDEPENDENT REVIEW VERDICT on the paused head — CHANGES-REQUESTED at 75d5677246469b80ab7949d8e95725431d456471 (reviewer surface:367, delivered after the pause). This CONFIRMS all four blockers on the evidence, and is more precise than the pause note in three places. Read it alongside the handoff.

CONFIRMED, with the reviewer's own measurements:
1. CROSS-TENANT (org-activity.ts:179-197; people.routes.ts:894-900) - check-then-read. A GET for an org-A person passes requirePerson, then all three UNION arms query by person_id/entity_id alone. The schema does not constrain audit_log.entity_id to the row's org. MEASURED: an org-B audit row targeting the org-A person ID is returned to org A, INCLUDING THE ORG-B ACTOR AND ACTION. Scope each arm in SQL; the precheck does not scope returned rows.
2. APPEND-ONLY IS FALSE (delete-event.ts:254-269) - deleting a demo event with removeDemoPeople=true runs UPDATE audit_log SET actor_person_id=NULL, so an existing fact that named its actor loses attribution. The row's evidentiary contents change rather than only new facts being appended.
3. PAGING (org-activity.ts:156-157,231-235; history.ts:165-166; PersonDrawer.tsx:87-95; SubmissionRecordPage.tsx:534-543) - concrete trace: page 1 = [A,B]; append X; page 2 becomes [B,C]. Person and submission lenses compare page 2 only with olderActivity/olderHistory and not page 1, so they render B TWICE and can declare Complete from the stale total while omitting X and D. The org lens dedupes B but finishes 4 of 5 and PERMANENTLY OMITS X. The new test fetches consecutive pages with no intervening append, so it cannot catch this.
4. QUEUE ADMISSION SHOWN AS DELIVERY (comms.routes.ts:830-842,865-909; activity-copy.ts:82-84) - POST /comms/send writes submission.message_sent immediately after enqueue, before the consumer sends. A demo-suppressed or downstream-failed outbox row leaves the timeline saying 'Message sent'. submission.decision_resent carries the same false claim when outbox_inserted=false.

VERIFIED NON-FINDINGS - these are SOUND and whoever resumes should NOT re-derive them:
- the migration backfill derives each surviving row's actual event org and leaves already-deleted-event rows NULL; org equality reads exclude NULL
- scripts/schema-verify.mjs changes ONLY 106 -> 107; check:schema passes at 53 tables / 134 indexes / 107 FKs / 3 triggers; audit_log_0021_new is unique AND ends in _new
- the rebase preserved #259 and #264's seams and both review.routes imports; no tests/node revert
- the new tests are behavioural, claim MRQ-211 only, and the org-route test fails on parent f83406e8 for the intended 404-vs-200 missing-lens reason

Validation at that head: three typechecks pass, node tests 239/239, activity-lenses Vitest 8/8, trace:ac merged pass, hosted fast-gate SUCCESS and PR CLEAN. No merge, push or source edit was performed by the reviewer.

NOTE FOR WHOEVER RESUMES: the PR reads CLEAN + fast-gate SUCCESS. It is not mergeable - none of the four failures reddens a gate. The [PAUSED] title and this ticket's blocked status are the only things standing between that green checkmark and a cross-tenant leak on main.
